To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TRW can be circumvented if the attacker knows that TRWs is being employed.

1) TRW can be circumvented by an adversary that has prior knowledge of TRW's detection algorithm; 2) circumvention can occur through a variety of means including full horizontal and full vertical scans; 3) the cost of circumvention is increased significantly with the use of the proposed TRW enhancements; and 4) the cost of detection can be reduced by using the proposed TRW optimizations.

TRW, as originally proposed, is vulnerable to circumvention through collaborative scanning, which is not detectable by the original algorithm; and, the 3 mitigations proposed in this paper, while increasing the cost of circumvention, are not perfect and do not eliminate the possibility of circumvention through collaborative scan.
